_comment: Food model (DESIGN §4.2, §3.1). 1 food = one person fed for one month. Yields are people fed PER YEAR by a fully worked hex; 'hands' = working hands needed to work it fully; output scales linearly with hands. Omer-approved STARTING VALUES for tuning (2026-11-04). MODEL SCALE ×3 (DESIGN §5.8, Omer 2026-11-04): every yield and every hands figure here, every building's hands in data/buildings.json, and all unit/settler sizes are 3× the original draft, so that a village crosses the 1,500 town gate and a town the 6,000 city gate by growth. The model is linear in population, so the curves are unchanged — only the labels (tests/scale.test.ts proves it).

harvest._comment: share of the yearly farming output arriving in each month (0 = January). Sums to 1.

variance._comment: DECIDED by Omer 2026-11-05 at sd 0.125 (a compromise between 0.10 and 0.15): each year every settlement's farming output is multiplied by a harvest factor drawn in January — 1 + sd × noise, floored at minFactor. regionalShare of the variance is shared by every settlement in the same regionSize×regionSize block of hexes (a bad year is regional, not private); the rest is local. sd 0 turns it off. Forecasts assume an average year, so a bad harvest surprises a settlement the way it should.

herding._comment: indexed by terrain pasture level 0–4; arrives monthly in twelfths

fishing._comment: Lake, River and shore (sea touching land) hexes. Offshore sea needs a port (later). With a Fish resource the richer row applies instead. Arrives monthly in twelfths.

hunting._comment: Game resource on a worked hex. Arrives monthly in twelfths.

granary._comment: Every settlement has one (DESIGN §3.3). capacity in months of the settlement's monthly consumption; spoilage = share of stock lost per month. Linear between unstaffed and fully staffed.

sharing._comment: A subordinate settlement keeps what it will eat until the next harvest PLUS this many months, and sends the rest to its parent each month; the parent takes what it has room for.
sharing._titheComment: DECIDED 2026-11-05 (DESIGN §4.2): the parent takes this share of every subordinate's food production in kind, the moment it is produced, before the subordinate reckons its own needs. 0.10 = customary tithe (draft). Must become a player policy (light / customary / heavy) with DESIGN §4.3.

privateEconomy._comment: DECIDED by Omer 2026-11-05 (Session 11b, DESIGN §4.2b; numbers DRAFT, ×3 scale). In the listed tiers every hand not in a building or a field is a PRIVATE hand — artisans, labourers, traders — and the crown sees it as revenue: each produces taxPerHandPerYear coins into the faction treasury and goodsPerHandPerYear goods into its settlement's stock (pooled by the cluster), by itself, with no building. Both are multiplied by administration quality (the hall's staffing for now; institutions, the tax-regime policy and public order later). Using private hands costs that tax: hands drawn to the building site or to gathering pay nothing while they work there (gathering counted as drawn is a PLACEHOLDER reading — Omer named construction, levies, settlers and work-bands). salesSharePerYear: every settlement of these tiers sells that share of its CLUSTER's goods a year into the treasury at goodsPrice, on its own (petty trade); a Market adds its salesShareBonus. Pricing: 0.2 coins/hand/yr makes a town of ~10,000 (≈3,800 private hands) worth ~750 coins a year — one modest building (DESIGN §3.3). Villages have spare hands, not private hands (peasants).

materials._comment: DECIDED by Omer 2026-11-05 (Session 11; numbers DRAFT, ×3 scale): timber and stone are gathered by the SPARE hands — the hands the food jobs do not need — so gathering never costs food; spare hands still count as spare for the crowding rule. Timber comes from the terrain's timber yield (0–4) of worked hexes, stone from worked Stone hexes (quarries and lumber camps multiply this in Phase 2). Units are abstract (a Mill costs 90 timber). Every settlement gathers into its own stock; the CLUSTER's stockpile is the sum over its members and building projects draw from it (DESIGN §4.2). STOCKPILE CAPS (Session 11b, replacing the flat December surplus share): a cluster's stockpile holds at most cap.base + cap.perSettlement × members of each material, plus what its Warehouses add (data/buildings.json stockCap); anything above that flows each month to the faction (realm) stockpile, which holds at most realmCap (to be set by administration quality, DESIGN §4.3 — a flat draft until then); above that it is lost. The player ships from the realm stockpile anywhere (instantly for now — PLACEHOLDER until roads and caravans).

construction._comment: A project advances by (spare hands given / buildHands) / buildMonths each month, capped at full speed. Spare hands go to construction before gathering.
